data.name: Dushala
data.long_meaning: Dushala is a name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘duhsala’ which means ‘difficult’ or ‘afflicted’. In Hindu mythology, Dushala is the name of a princess who was cursed by the sage Durvasa due to her mother's disrespect towards him. Despite her difficult circumstances, Dushala is remembered for her unwavering devotion to Lord Rama and her compassion towards those in need.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Dushala's name represents the spiritual truth that even in the face of great affliction and adversity, one can find inner peace and devotion to God. Her story serves as a reminder that no matter what life throws our way, we have the capacity to remain steadfast in our faith and maintain compassion for others. Additionally, Dushala's unwavering devotion to Lord Rama demonstrates the power of unconditional love and devotion to a higher power, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.

historical_references.reference: Dushala was the wife of King Shalva of Haihayas. She was the mother of Bhishma, the great grand-father of Pandava brothers. Dushala's story is narrated in the Mahabharata.

Dushala was also the name of a princess in the Gupta Empire who was the mother of Harshavardhana, the famous emperor. During Harshavardhana's reign, the empire reached its peak and came to be known as the Harshavardhana Empire.
